initiative.title: explorEDA runtime modes
initiative.summary: Run one standalone explorEDA app in four modes — browser-only, local CLI, self-hosted Docker Compose, and paid per-tenant hosting — over one storage model whose backing store changes per mode.
initiative.next_action: Execute the local CLI implementation plan (local-cli-projects M1).

sources.notes: Hosting-modes initiative somewhat replaces the commercialization initiative, possibly in parallel; separate initiative for a proper app with users, login, config.
No CLI, server, auth, or user model exists.

claims.statement: explorEDA runs as a standalone app in several runtime modes, separate from the embeddable component.
Modes ordered by administration: browser-only, local CLI, self-hosted Docker Compose, paid per-tenant hosting; paid comes after the others work.
Config and settings state is unified across modes: app config, user data, project/workspace files, data-source info, common schema info, notebooks or standalone results.
Embedded component: the host developer handles storage, users, and data.
The 'hosted' app, currently the demo, becomes a standalone app.
Project/workspace files on disk; data-source info in a database.
Database sources require a server; browser-only is file/CSV only.
This program somewhat replaces commercial-license (component licensing on unmerged claude/license-* branches) and may run in parallel with it.
claims.confidence: high for which initiative; degree of replacement open

claims.statement: Mode differences belong in storage, auth, and data-source adapters, not separate app forks.
Local CLI is the first mode to build.
Five initiatives: runtime-modes umbrella, standalone-app, browser-only-site, local-cli-projects, self-hosted-team-server.
One Node server package serves CLI and self-hosted modes; modes differ by storage, auth, and data-source adapters.
Pause commercial-license; revenue is expected from hosted and self-hosted app plans.
customer-instance-hosting was a seed for this program; it is paused and merges in when managed (paid) servers are shaped.
exploreda.dev browser-only mode stays the demo; apps/app is the server-backed app for CLI, self-hosted, and managed modes.
Self-hosting is free; revenue comes from the paid managed tier.
Near-term goal: a public npx exploreda launch.
The CLI project-folder format is shared: the demo can open a project folder via File System Access.
The project-folder format is built inside the CLI's first milestone, on DSL v2; sources, joins, and analyses are all text.

history.summary: Intent recovered from two handwritten notebook pages and the accompanying chat request.
local-cli-projects shaped; folder format resolved as part of CLI M1 on DSL v2; static export dropped from CLI v1.

related_initiatives.role: component licensing (unmerged branches claude/license-1..5); partly replaced, may run in parallel

question_rounds.focus: scope and splits across runtime modes

questions.question: How does customer-instance-hosting relate to runtime-modes?
questions.effect: The commercialization initiative is commercial-license (unmerged claude/license-* branches: offline keys, Paddle, license service for the component). customer-instance-hosting relation re-asked in round 2.

questions.question: Which mode first?
questions.effect: local-cli-projects leads; it builds the first server and files-on-disk project storage.

questions.question: Where does the standalone app come from?
questions.effect: Demo stays the landing/docs/examples site; apps/app hosts the component through storage and auth ports.

questions.question: Is the five-initiative split right?
questions.effect: No merge.

questions.question: Should the self-hosted image run the CLI's server?
questions.effect: One Node server package; CLI and Docker differ by storage, auth, and source adapters.

questions.question: How do runtime modes relate to commercial-license?
questions.effect: commercial-license (unmerged claude/license-* branches) is paused; revenue is expected from hosted/self-hosted app plans.

questions.question: What happens to customer-instance-hosting?
questions.answer: It was a starter seed for this modes work; it has useful info on where to host managed versions. Pause it or merge it in when we reach managed servers.
questions.effect: customer-instance-hosting paused; merge into runtime-modes at the managed (paid) server stage.

questions.question: Database sources in the first CLI release?
questions.effect: CLI v1 is file-only; DB connections are the next CLI milestone reusing database-adapters.

questions.question: Which package ships the CLI and server?
questions.effect: npx exploreda runs from the component package; server code must not burden component consumers (provisional default: bundle the server into the bin build).

questions.question: How does a CLI project store analyses on disk?
questions.answer: Config storable in either a hidden folder or analysis workspace files. A project folder with common info and a file per analysis, similar to notebooks.
questions.effect: Project folder = shared project info + one file per analysis. Meaning of 'either' clarified in round 3.

questions.question: No sign-in in CLI; accounts built for self-hosted?
questions.effect: standalone-app ships a single-local-user auth adapter first.

questions.question: Does exploreda.dev run apps/app or stay the demo?
questions.effect: Browser-only mode is the improved demo; apps/app is server-backed (CLI, self-hosted, managed).

questions.question: Config in hidden folder or workspace files — which reading?
questions.effect: CLI supports both layouts: all config hidden in .exploreda/ or visible project/workspace files.

questions.question: Should the demo read/write the CLI project-folder format?
questions.effect: Demo opens a CLI project folder in Chromium via File System Access; same analysis files.

questions.question: How do self-hosted viewers get in?
questions.effect: Viewers sign in with a viewer role; no anonymous share links in the first self-hosted release.

questions.question: First self-hosted sign-in method?
questions.effect: Admin-managed email + password; OIDC/SSO later (managed tier).

questions.question: What else is in CLI v1?
questions.answer: Global config, file watching, static export.
questions.effect: Notebook view excluded from CLI v1; it follows notebook-analysis.

questions.question: Is self-hosting paid?
questions.effect: Docker Compose is free; revenue from the managed tier.

questions.question: Data files read in place with project-relative paths?
questions.effect: Relative paths by default; absolute paths to outside files are allowed and flagged as non-portable.

questions.question: Near-term goal?
questions.effect: CLI must be polished enough to announce: install, first-run, docs, and stable file format.
